jobs.description: The SOS Children's Villages worldwide Hermann-Gmeiner-Fonds Deutschland e.V. is an independent, non-denominational children's rights organization. With its headquarters in Munich and offices in Berlin and Düsseldorf, the organization has been supporting the global projects of SOS Children's Villages since 1963. 200 employees are committed to the vision of "For a world that lets you grow". With almost 3,000 programs in over 130 countries, the organization offers help to children, young people and families in need through education, medical care and family strengthening. The focus is on strengthening the family, sustainability, children's rights and cultural sensitivity.   To support our Scholarships & Educational Development team in our Munich office, we are looking for a (Junior) Program Manager - Scholar Support & Quality (m/f/d) on a full time basis. Your tasks As (Junior) Program Manager - Scholar Support & Quality, take operational ownership of scholar support, program quality, and MEAL within the Global Scholarship Program (GSP). You work closely with scholars, colleagues, and external partners to ensure that scholars receive appropriate support, cases are well documented, program standards are upheld, risks and concerns are managed appropriately, and evidence and learning are systematically used to strengthen the program. This includes the following tasks: Program Quality, MEAL & Impact: Develop & manage a safeguarding-informed GSP quality and MEAL framework. Coordinate data collection, analysis and reporting and ensure findings are translated into concrete program improvements. Coordinate impact measurement approaches, including SROI, and lead the preparation of the GSP annual report. Provide administrative support to the team Scholar Support & Documentation: Manage and coordinate the scholar support process throughout their journey. Maintain and update scholar information as well as all relevant documents (communications, reports, transcripts) in appropriate databases and tools. Schedule check-ins & respond promptly to general inquiries from students and stakeholders. Serve as the primary contact for scholar inquiries on YouthLinks Community (an internal communication platform), by coordinating, developing, and posting relevant information, guidance, and support materials for scholars. Prepare reports as required        Your profile You have successfully completed studies in social work, psychology, youth development, social sciences, education, international development, public policy or a related field. You bring initial relevant professional experience in one or more areas such as student or youth support, program quality, monitoring and evaluation. Skills in MHPSS are an advantage. You are highly organized and approach routine and recurring tasks with diligence and understand their importance for effective scholar support, monitoring and program management. You are proactive and bring forward innovative ideas for improvements. You are a team player with a positive attitude, hands-on-mentality and get things done. You are flexible in navigating a complex and fast changing environment and have the ability to prioritize effectively when faced with multiple requests. You have effective communication skills with excellent command of English. Another foreign language such as Spanish, Portuguese, German, Arabic or French is an advantage. You have very good skills in MS-Office, Adobe & Canva. Additional computer skills are a plus. We offer A diverse, inspiring, and responsible role in a professionally managed, internationally active non-profit organization·       Opportunities for professional development and the chance to be part of an international network An open ear for new ideas and impulses, and the opportunity to help shape our work Work-life balance through flexible working hours, compensatory time off, and the option to work remotely (including from abroad) Numerous benefits like employer funded pension and financial allowance for childcare Meal allowance, subsidy for the Deutschlandticket, subsidized EGYM Wellpass Interesting further training opportunities SOS Children's Villages adhere to strict child safeguarding principles and maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse. Therefore, during recruitment, we not only consider personal and professional suitability, but also the willingness to act according to our child protection guidelines and values. We require an extended police clearance certificate upon employment. Diversity is important to us. At SOS Children's Villages Worldwide, we actively stand against racism and discrimination, and we welcome applications from people regardless of their ethnic, national, or social background, gender, disability, age, or sexual orientation. If you are excited about this challenging role, we look forward to receiving your application soon! SOS-Kinderdörfer weltweit  Ridlerstr. 55 80339 München

jobs.employer_name: Max-Planck-Institut für die Physik des Lichts
jobs.description:
About us

The Max-Planck-Zentrum für Physik und Medizin (MPZPM) is an interdisciplinary joint research center of the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light (MPL), Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), and Universitätsklinikum Erlangen (UKER). Research at MPZPM addresses fundamental questions in medicine, aiming to understand living systems, biological processes, and their pathological changes from a novel physical perspective.

Facility Leader - Lab-on-a-Chip (LoC) Facility at MPZPM
Core Facilities (CF) at MPZPM provide cutting-edge technologies and form an essential part of the center’s scientific infrastructure. The Lab-on-a-Chip (LoC) Facility is equipped with state-of-the-art microfabrication technologies housed within a cleanroom at MPZPM. LoC can also draw on the capabilities of another nanofabrication cleanroom facility at MPL. The unit supports researchers in developing advanced microfluidic chips, microtools and physiologically relevant microenvironments for studies at the interface of physics and medicine. We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Facility Head to manage and further develop the Lab-on-a-Chip facility. You will oversee daily operations, ensure safe and efficient laboratory workflows, support scientific users from diverse backgrounds and contribute to the design and development of innovative methodologies.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Management

Lead, mentor, and support scientific and technical staff, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team.
Oversee facility operations, including planning, budgeting, maintenance, and strategic development.
Train and support users from diverse scientific backgrounds.

Technical Expertise & Scientific Support

Ensure reliable operation of cleanroom infrastructure and microfabrication equipment.
Provide expert guidance in microfabrication, microfluidics, and lab-on-a-chip system development.
Contribute to the development of new microstructured materials, microfluidic chips, and advanced LoC technologies.

Innovation & Development

Support interdisciplinary research projects and facilitate knowledge transfer across scientific fields.
Develop novel microfluidics-based methodologies and provide SOPs to ensure reliable and reproducible use.
Propose and discuss organizational and infrastructure improvements with the MPZPM board, focusing on optimized workflows, state-of-the-art technologies, and strategic upgrades aligned with the institute’s priorities.
You bring:

MSc or PhD in physics, biophysics, chemistry, materials science, biomedical engineering, or a related field.
Experience in managing laboratories, particularly cleanrooms, including staff supervision and operation of microfabrication workflows.
Strong organizational, leadership, and project-management skills, with a track record of building or expanding scientific infrastructure.
Expertise in developing microfluidic technologies.
Capability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary and multicultural environment.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across scientific disciplines. English is the primary working language; knowledge of German is advantageous.
Experience in technology transfer, device development, or industry collaboration is a plus.

Ideal Technical Competencies (some of the following):

Microfabrication & Lithography: photolithography, soft lithography, micropatterning of rigid and soft materials, biomolecule patterning via microcontact printing or LIMA photopatterning.
Microfluidics & Lab-on-a-Chip Systems: design, production, and integration of microfluidic chips with fluidic, optical and electronic components.
Soft Material Microstructuring: hydrogels, droplet microfluidics, and other soft materials relevant to biomedical applications.
3D structuring using Digital Light Processing (DLP) and Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM).

The Max Planck Society for the Advancement of Science (Max Planck Gesellschaft, MPG) is a self-governing scientific organization funded by the Federal and State Governments. It conducts basic research in the fields of natural sciences, the humanities and the social sciences in 85 institutes and research units in Germany and abroad.

The MPG consists of three sections: the Biology and Medicine Section, the Chemistry, Physics and Technology Section and the Human Sciences Section. Each section has a Scientific Scouting Officer who supports the respective section and its institutes in identifying the next generation of leading researchers.

For the Human Sciences Section, the Administrative Headquarters of the MPG are now seeking a:

Scientific Scouting Officer (all genders) -

80% part-time initially, with a potential full-time transition effective 1 January 2029

(Reference Number 63/26)

to start as early as possible.

The Section includes a range of disciplines, notably the History of Art, Anthropology, Demography, Economics, the History of Science, Law, Neurosciences, Political Sciences, Psychology, and Sociology.

Proactive and systematic identification of outstanding scientists to support the Human Sciences Section and its Core and Appointment Commissions
Building and analyzing candidate pools, generating appropriate statistics
Using various talent acquisition tools, including but not limited to internet sourcing, data mining, social media, networking at national and international conferences, as well as other creative methods to identify outstanding candidates
Analyzing candidate lists generated through nomination calls
Implementing, maintaining and further developing candidate databases together with the two Scouting Officers of the other section
Attending international conferences, participating in public outreach to promote the MPG
Complementing the current scouting team and actively participating in constantly developing the team’s scouting concept, tackling human sciences-oriented as well as interdisciplinary scouting projects

Doctoral degree in one of the scientific disciplines of the Human Sciences Section and several years of postdoctoral experience
Education and/or postdoctoral research abroad, ideally for several years
In-depth knowledge of the German and international research landscape (including organizational and research-specific framework conditions)
Proven scientific track record and demonstrated knowledge of the respective scientific community
General interest in a broad range of scientific subjects covered in the Human Sciences Section and ability to quickly familiarize yourself with new areas of research
Solution-oriented, service-driven, creative and open-minded working style
Excellent proficiency in English (written and spoken, level C1-C2) and good proficiency in German (minimum level B2)
Excellent interpersonal communication and networking skills, in order to interact with and coordinate partners with diverse professional and multicultural backgrounds
Experience in working with AI applications or a willingness to learn how to use such systems
Willingness to adopt flexible working hours, as well as taking part in regular business travel in Germany and abroad
Experience in scouting/recruiting scientists would be desirable

You will gain fascinating insights into the outstanding research at our Max Planck Institutes.
You will help to identify the next generation of outstanding scientists for the MPG by directly interacting with its leadership and directors.
As a member of the Section Office, you will cooperate with the department "Institutes" at the Administrative Headquarters of the MPG.

Your creative fieldWe are looking for a full-time, permanent Senior QA Engineer (all genders) to start as soon as possible . We live remote-first within Germany, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations.

Contabo serves 180,000+ customers worldwide across VPS, dedicated servers, object storage and a growing cloud-native platform. Quality isn't a bottleneck function here – it's embedded in how we build.
You'll work across multiple development teams on products that vary significantly in architecture, maturity and risk profile. The scope is wide and the technical surface is real.

QA here means jumping between contexts and figuring things out, not just executing scripts against a stable codebase.
You come in before development starts: read the requirements, flag what's untestable and push back early.
You own the test strategy and update it as things change – not as a document exercise, but because the products actually change.

You write test plans and test cases, run manual tests (functional, regression, exploratory, UAT) and build and maintain automated tests across UI, API and integration.
We use AI tools actively: in development, in testing, in how we work day to day and we expect the same from you. That's not a trend we're chasing: it's how we stay fast without cutting corners on quality.

You keep the continuous testing pipelines running and help the teams use them. When bugs come up, you write bug reports that developers can actually work with – reproduction steps, impact, everything needed to close it without a follow-up ping.
Regular regression cycles after major releases are part of the job, as is running UAT with product stakeholders.

What convinces usYour personality, paired with:
• 5+ years in software testing/QA, ideally in agile teams
• Test automation in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript; hands-on with frameworks like Playwright, Frisby, or Supertest
• Experience using AI-assisted tools in development or testing (AI code generators, LLM-based test support or similar) and comfortable using Claude (or comparable LLMs) as part of your daily workflow
• Solid grasp of test design, QA processes, and translating requirements into test plans and test cases
• API testing (REST), Git, bug tracking, browser DevTools – these are daily tools for you
• Comfortable prioritizing across multiple test streams simultaneously
• Fluent English skills and German language skills would be a plus
• Experience with AI-assisted tools in testing or development
• UAT facilitation, QA process ownership, performance/integration testing

We know that you may not currently meet all the requirements. But if you come to us with the right amount of commitment and enthusiasm, we can take off together and make a big difference.

Awesome ProspectsAt Contabo, we are constantly evolving. Our growth creates space for new ideas, ownership, and real impact for people who want to make a difference.
What defines us is trust, direct communication, and an open feedback culture. We believe the best solutions are built together and that everyone has the opportunity to contribute, grow, and leave their own footprint.
Additionally, we offer:
• Work the way that fits your life – Remote or hybrid with flexible hours for a healthy work-life balance and the same technical equipment at home as in the office
• Experience real freedom – Workation across the EU and in our summer office in Mallorca
• Stay active and healthy – Access to EGYM Wellpass and thousands of fitness and wellness facilities
• Enjoy exclusive perks – Attractive discounts on many products and services through our corporate benefits program
• Recharge your energy – 30 days of vacation plus additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve
• Give back – An extra day off to get involved in social activities through our Volunteer Day
• Make an impact – Take ownership and bring your ideas to life with real creative freedom
• Keep growing – Individual professional and personal development opportunities in an innovative tech environment
• Feel comfortable where you work – Modern, conveniently located offices across our European locations
• Be part of a diverse team – Work in an international environment shaped by diversity
• Create lasting memories – Company events and team activities you won’t forget

How to reach usIf you have any questions, you can reach out to Alina by email at alina.peissl@contabo.de.

jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Tasks & responsibilities

- Your primary responsibilities will include coordinating, evaluating, and conducting in silico assessments to predict mutagenicity in accordance with ICH M7, including the scientific evaluation of related literature searches.
- In close collaboration with i internal and external stakeholders, you will develop and support derisking strategies for mutagenic impurities and metabolites across different stages of project development.
- Furthermore, you will prepare scientific reports, including expert judgment on the relevance of findings, and contribute to regulatory submission documents.
- As a subject matter expert, you will advise Research & Development teams on mutagenic impurities, mutagenic metabolites, and acceptable exposure limits for mutagenic carcinogens.
- In addition, you will represent scientific results and recommendations in international project teams, discuss their implications, and support informed risk-based decision-making.
- You will also independently manage and respond to health authority inquiries related to ICH M7 topics, coordinate global project requirements, and ensure compliance with regulatory expectations and internal procedures.

Additional tasks for the Senior Principal Scientist-Role

- With regard to the global genotoxicity strategy, you will take a leading role in its implementation and further development to ensure the application of avoidance principles and scientifically sound risk assessments.
- Moreover, you will lead complex and time-critical issues with significant regulatory impact and provide recommendations to international stakeholders.
- Additionally, you will contribute to scientific committees and expert forums, foster scientific exchange, and drive the advancement of scientific standards and best practices.

Requirements

- PhD in Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry Eor comparable scientific degree with relevant professional experience, or Master's degree in Biology or Computer Science
- Solid knowledge of mutagenicity, structural reactivity, and genetic toxicology
- Expertise in in silico mutagenicity prediction, including relevant software tools, derisking strategies, and associated genetic toxicology assays
- Experience in literature research and the use of scientific databases
- Knowledge of pharmaceutical development and the application of genetic toxicology principles in a drug development environment
- Ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders, work effectively under pressure, and communicate complex scientific findings in German and English

Additional requirements for the Senior Principal Scientist-Role

- Extensive experience in applying and interpreting in silico mutagenicity assessments within pharmaceutical development
- Demonstrated capability to lead complex scientific topics and coordinate cross-functional global stakeholders
- Experience in representing scientific positions in interactions with health authorities, scientific committees, or expert forums

As part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.
Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. In cases of equal qualifications, such applicants will be given preferential consideration in the selection process.
With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team, Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or via mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.com
